Thus queens in consecutive rows cannot occupy columns differing by 1." This is a specific non-attacking constraint often called "no-touching". It's stricter than standard N-queens for adjacent rows but looser for distant rows ("Queens separated by more than one row MAY share a long diagonal"). So, standard chess queen moves don't apply globally, only the local adjacency rule.
